hero.accroche: How far have you actually gone?
hero.description: The purity test is 50 questions about what you've already done: nights out, exes, lies, sex, and so on. Take it solo for your own score, or together to rate your couple, then compare with your partner!

s1.titre: What is a purity test, exactly?
s1.lead: A purity test is a long list of things people do, and you tick the ones you've already done. The more boxes you tick, the higher your score goes, and the less "pure" you are.
s1.p1: The best-known one, the Rice Purity Test, comes from Rice University in Texas, and it has been all over social media. If the idea works so well as a party game, it's mostly because you end up with a number you can compare with your friends, or with your boyfriend or girlfriend.
s1.p2: Our version has two modes. Solo, the questions are about you: your exes, your lies, the nights that got out of hand, or what you've hidden from someone. As a couple, they're about your relationship, what you've done together and what you've kept from each other.
s1.sub1Titre: Why it works so well as a pair
s1.sub1P1: A score is easy to compare. You each take the test on your own, send each other your results, and the conversation starts by itself. Most of the time you end up talking less about the number than about the question that made someone pause, and from there you quickly get to questions you never ask each other.

s2.p1: Not every question is worth the same number of points. If every ticked box were worth one point, almost everyone would end up with an average score, and the result wouldn't mean much. For example:

lignes: Leaving a party without telling anyone
Doing it in public, where you could have been seen
tableau.note: A daft moment at a party and something that can kill someone shouldn't weigh the same.

s2.p2: Each question also offers three to five degrees instead of a yes or a no. « Have you ever cheated on someone? » doesn't call for the same answer depending on whether it was a kiss at a party or a six-month double life, and the scale reflects that.

encart.titre: The maximum changes with the version
encart.texte: The full version reaches 899 points solo and 927 as a couple. The all-audiences version, served to anyone who says they're under 16, drops the explicit questions and therefore caps lower. The verdict is worked out as a percentage of the maximum actually played, otherwise the shorter version would be condemned to stay tame.

s3.p1: The two modes don't ask the same questions and don't score the same thing. Choose before you start, you can't switch halfway.

comparatif.texte: The questions are about you. Your past, your exes, what you hid, what you never told anyone. This is the mode to pick if you want to send your score and dare someone to match it.

It's no longer two people being scored, it's one story: what you did together, where you did it, and what you kept from each other. Answers are said out loud, which makes this mode considerably more dangerous.

s3.p2: The couple mode doesn't overlap with the couple test: one measures what you've done together, the other where your relationship stands today. Doing both back to back gives two very different readings of the same couple.

encart.titre: One piece of advice before starting couple mode
encart.texte: Some questions ask you to say out loud things that have never been said. If the subject is still raw between you, take the solo mode separately and compare nothing but the scores. The number is enough to start the discussion without forcing anyone into detail.

s4.p1: Questions are split into categories, and the result breaks your score down for each one. That's usually where the surprise turns up: you think you're well behaved because the total is average, and you discover you're at 90% in a single family.
liste1: 💔 Cheating: from a kiss at a party to a double life
🎭 Lies: what you tidied up, left out, deleted
🍸 Booze & co: nights out, excess, and what comes with it
📱 Online life: nudes, secret accounts, morning-after messages
s4.sub1P1: The breakdown often holds surprises: you can have a reasonable score on sex and blow the counter on lies, or the other way round.
liste2: 👀 Getting caught: the risk of being seen, owned or not
🍸 Substances: nights out, being under the influence, the morning after
🚨 Crossing lines: casinos, off-limits places, lies told together
🤐 Secrets: what the other one still doesn't know
s4.sub2P1: The secrets category scores what one of you has hidden from the other. So two couples who've lived roughly the same things can end up with very different scores.

s5.citation: A high score just means you've been through quite a lot, not that you're a bad person.
s5.p1: Some of it is memories from nights out and some of it is mistakes, and the test doesn't tell them apart: it adds up points. It's up to you to decide what the number says.
s5.p2: Where the result gets interesting is when two people compare it. Three hundred points between two partners isn't a problem in itself, but it sometimes explains tensions nobody could put a name on. On the other hand, two close scores don't mean you agree on your values and your plans: the purity test only looks at the past.

encart.titre: And if the other person's score hurts
encart.texte: It happens. The test covers a whole past, and most of it often happened before you. What helps most is what the person is willing to tell you behind the number.

faq.a1: Yes, completely. There's no account to create, no email to give and no paid version: you answer the questions and your score shows up at the end.
faq.a2: No. No individual answer is kept. Only the final score is recorded, with nothing that could point back to you, and it only serves to work out the average and the curve shown on the page.
faq.a3: Five to seven minutes for the fifty questions solo. As a couple it takes longer, because you'll definitely stop to talk about it!
faq.q4: What counts as a good score?
faq.a4: There isn't one. Most people land between 25 and 40% of the maximum, so a result around 250 to 350 points. Below that you're very well behaved, above it you have a history, but neither is better than the other.
faq.q5: Can more than two people play?
faq.a5: Couple mode is built for two. Nothing stops a whole group from taking the solo mode separately and comparing scores afterwards though: that's the best use of the test when there are several of you.
faq.a6: The test asks your age before it starts. Under 16, it switches to an all-audiences version, which removes the questions about explicit sex and drugs and keeps everything about lies, family, nights out and secrets. For a teen couple, the teen couple quiz is probably a better fit.
